x: The statement in the interpretation of the surah in which iron is mentioned Meaning, the Most High, by His saying:
h
Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies God

, that everything below Him of His creation glorifies Him in reverence for Him, acknowledging His Lordship, and submitting to His obedience, as the Most High said: “The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is therein glorify Him.

There is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise, but you do not understand their glorification.” (al-Isra’ 17:44) And His statement, And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise, means: But He, may His glory be exalted, is the Exalted in His vengeance upon those who disobeyed Him and violated His command from among His creation in the heavens and the earth. The Wise in His management of their affairs and His disposition of them as He willed and loved.
And His statement,
h
To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth

, God Almighty says: He has authority over the heavens and the earth and everything in them, and nothing in them is able to resist Him. He has authority over all of them and His judgment is carried out. And His statement,
h
He gives life and causes death

, means: He gives life to whatever He wills of creation by creating it however He wills, by creating from the dead sperm an animal by breathing the spirit into it after a few times in which He turns it over and other things like that, and He causes to death whatever He wills of the living after life, after it has reached its appointed time, so He annihilates it. And He is over all things competent, means, may His praise be exalted, He is over all things competent, and nothing He wills of giving life and causing death, honoring and humiliating, and other matters is impossible for Him. .

God Almighty says: He is the First before everything without limit. And the Last means: The Last is after everything without end. It was said thus because He was and nothing existed besides Him. He will be after the annihilation of all things, as He, the Most High, said: Everything will perish except His Face (al-Qasas 28:88). And His statement: And the Manifest means: He is the Manifest over everything below Him. He is the High above everything, so nothing is higher than Him. And the Hidden means: He is the Hidden of all things, so nothing is closer to anything than Him, as He said:
And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein
In a similar manner to what we said about that, the report came from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people of interpretation said the same.
Mention of who said that and the report that was narrated about it:

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
He is the First and the Last

, the Evident and the Immanent, it was mentioned to us that while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting among his companions, a cloud rose up against them. He said, Do you know what this is? They said, God and His Messenger know best. He said, Indeed, it is the firm, restrained wave and a protected ceiling. He said, Do you know how much is between you and it? They said, God and His Messenger know best. He said, A journey of five hundred years. He said, Do you know what is above that? They said, Likewise. He said, “Above it is another heaven, and between them is a ... the Throne, and between it and the seventh heaven is like what is between two heavens.” He said, Do you know what is below you? They said, God and His Messenger know best. He said, It is the earth. He said, Do you know what is below it? They said, Likewise, it is the earth. He said, Do you know what is below it? They said, It is the same as their first statement. He said, Below it is another earth, and between them is a journey of five hundred years, until he enumerated seven earths, and between every two earths is a journey of five hundred years. Then he said, “By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, if one of you were let down by a rope to The other earth to descend upon God then read “
h
He is the First and the Last
, the Evident and the Immanent, and He is Knowing of all things.” And His statement,
h
And He is All-Knowing of all things
, means that God Almighty says:
h
And He is All-Knowing of all things
. Nothing is hidden from Him, and not even the weight of an atom on earth or in heaven escapes Him, nor anything smaller than that or larger, except that it is in a clear book.

x: And His statement,
h
It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days

, God Almighty says: It is He who created the seven heavens and the earths, and administers them and what is in them, then He established Himself on His Throne, so He rose above it and was exalted above it. And His statement,
h
He knows what goes into the earth and what comes out of it

, says the Most High, informing about His description and that nothing of His creation is hidden from Him. He knows what goes into the earth of His creation, meaning by His statement, goes in, “enters,” and what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky to the earth of anything, and what ascends therein, and He is with you wherever you are, meaning, He is a witness for you, O people, wherever you are. He knows you and knows your deeds, your movements, and your resting place, and He is on His throne above His seven heavens. And God is Seeing, meaning, God is All-Seeing of your deeds that you do, of good and bad, obedience and disobedience. He is a Sight Seeer, and He is their keeper, so that He may reward the doer of good among you for his good and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing on the Day when it is recompensed. Every soul is for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged. (al-Jathiyah 45:22)

God Almighty says: He has authority over the heavens and the earth, effective over all of them and over all that is in them. His command is in them, and to God all matters return. He, the Most High, says: And to God all matters return. He, the Most High, says: And to God the fate of all His creation is, and He judges between them according to His judgment.
And His statement,
h
He causes the night to enter the day
, means by His statement,
h
He causes the night to enter the day

, that He includes whatever hours of the night are missing in the day, making them an increase in its hours. And He causes the day to enter the night, means: He includes whatever hours of the day are missing in the night, making them an increase in the hours of the night. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. We have mentioned the narration of what they said in the past in this book of ours, except that we will mention in this place what we did not mention there, God willing.

c: Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement,
h
He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night
, he said: The shortness of this is in the length of this and the length of this is in the shortness of this.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night
, he said: The night entering the day and the day entering the night.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement,
h
He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night

, he said: The shortness of the days of winter is due to the length of its nights, and the shortness of the nights of summer is due to the length of its days. And His statement, And He is All-Knowing of that within the breasts, means: He has knowledge of the secrets in the breasts of His servants and what their souls have resolved to do of good or evil or what their souls have thought of. Nothing of that is hidden from Him.

x: God Almighty says: Believe in God, O people, and acknowledge His Oneness and in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believe in what he brought you from God and follow him. And spend from that over which He has made you successors. God Almighty says: And spend from that over which God has given you wealth which He has inherited from those who came before you, and He has made you their successors in it, in the cause of God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding God’s statement, those who are successors therein, he said: Those who live long in it with provision. And His statement, Those of you who have believed and spent, means: Those of you, O people, who have believed in God and His Messenger and spent from what God has given them on behalf of those who came before them and provided them with money in the way of God, for them is a great reward, meaning for them is a great reward.

x: God Almighty says: And what is the matter with you that you do not believe in God? And what is the matter with you, O people, that you do not acknowledge the Oneness of God and His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, calls you to acknowledge His Oneness, and He has given you proofs of the truth of that which cut off your excuse and removed doubt from your hearts.
h
And He has taken your covenant
. It was said about me in that: And your Lord has taken your covenant from you in the loins of Adam that God is your Lord, there is no god for you other than Him.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And He has taken your covenant

, he said, on the back of Adam. The reciters differed in the recitation of this. The reciters of Hijaz and Iraq, other than Abu Amr, recited it as and He took your covenant with the opening of the alif from to take and the accusative of the covenant, meaning: and your Lord took your covenant. Abu Amr recited it as and He took your covenant with the damma of the alif and the nominative of the covenant, as if its agent was not named. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two readings with similar meanings, so whichever one the reader reads is correct, even though the opening of the alif in akhdha and the nasb of mithaq is more pleasing to me in this regard, due to the large number of readers who read that way and the small number of readers who read the other way. His saying,
h
If you are believers

, means: If you want to believe in God one day, then now is the most appropriate time for you to believe, so that the arguments will continue to be presented to you through the Messenger, his notification, and his calling you to what has been established as true for you through the notifications, evidence, and covenant taken from you.

Abu Amr recited it as and He took your covenant with the damma of the alif and the nominative of the covenant, as if its agent was not named.

x: God Almighty says: God is the One who sends down to His servant Muhammad clear verses, meaning detailed ones, to bring you out from darkness into the light. God Almighty says: To bring you out, O people, from the darkness of disbelief into the light of faith and from misguidance to guidance. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
From darkness to light

, he said: From misguidance to guidance. And His statement, And indeed, God is to you Most Kind and Most Merciful, God Almighty says: And indeed, God, by sending down to His servant what He sent down to him of clear verses to guide you and enlighten you to the right path, is most kind and merciful to you. So out of His kindness and mercy toward you, He did this.

x: God Almighty says: And what is the matter with you, O people, that you do not spend from what God has provided you in the way of God? And to God will return your wealth if you do not spend it during your life in the way of God. For to Him belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth. And He, the Most High, only urged them with that regarding their portion, saying to them: Spend your wealth in the way of God so that it may be a reserve for you with God before you die and are no longer able to do so, and the wealth becomes an inheritance for He to whom belong the heavens and the earth. And his saying:
h
Those of you who spent before the conquest and fought are not equal
. The commentators differed in their interpretation of this.
Some of them said that it means: Those of you who believed before the conquest of Mecca and emigrated are not equal.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought
, he said: He believed and spent, meaning: He who emigrated is not like he who did not emigrate.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest, meaning those who believed. He said: Mahran told us on the authority of Sufyan, who said: He says something else.

x: Others said that the conquest meant the conquest of Mecca and the expenditure in the jihad against the polytheists.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, “
h
Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought

. Those are greater in degree than those who spent and fought afterwards. But to all God has promised good.” He said: There were two fights, one of which was better than the other, and there were two expenditures, one of which was better than the other. The spending and fighting before the conquest the conquest of Mecca were better than the spending and fighting after that.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, before the conquest, he said: The conquest of Mecca.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Abdullah bin Ayyash told me: Zaid bin Aslam said
m: about this verse, Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest, he said: The conquest of Mecca.

x: Others said: What is meant by the opening in this place is the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.
Who said that?

c: Ishaq bin Shaheen told me: Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Amer, who said:
m: The separation between the two migrations was the conquest of Hudaybiyyah. God Almighty says:
h
Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought
. The verse.

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told me: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us: Dawud told us on the authority of ʿAmir
m: regarding this verse: Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest. He said: The conquest of al-Hudaybiyyah. He said: The separation between the two Umrahs was the conquest of al-Hudaybiyyah.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told me: Abdul-Wahhab told us: Dawud told us on the authority of Aamer:
m: The separation between the two migrations was the

x: God the Almighty says: Who is he who spends in the cause of God in this world, expecting reward in his spending, seeking what is with God? And that is the good loan. He says: So his Lord will multiply for him his loan, that which he lent him for his spending in His cause, and He will give him seven hundred for one.
Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say in his statement,
h
Who is he who would loan God a good loan

? It is like the Arabs’ saying: I have with you a loan of truth and a loan of evil, if he did good with it. And he recited a verse by Shanfara in this regard: We will reward Salaman bin Mufrij for what his hands have put forth, so he removed it. And he will have a noble reward.
And he will have a noble reward and recompense.
By that reward, he means Paradise. We have already mentioned the narration from the people of interpretation regarding that, and there is no need to repeat it.
The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of His statement,
h
On the Day you see the believing men and believing women
, their light proceeding before them and on their right.
Some of them said: The meaning of this is:
h
On the Day you see the believing men and believing women
, their light shining before them and on their right.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
On the Day you see the believing men and believing women

, the verse. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “Among the believers are those whose light will shine from Medina to Aden, Abyan, Sana’a, and beyond that, to the point that among the believers are those whose light will shine only where their feet are.”

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada,
m: something similar.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Idris told us:
m: I heard my father mention on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Qais bin Sakn, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: They will be given their light according to the extent of their deeds.

x: Some of them will be given their light like a palm tree, and some of them will be given their light like a standing man. The light of them with the light of the least of them will be on his thumb, sometimes it will be extinguished and sometimes it will be kindled.
Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is:
h
On the Day you see the believing men and believing women
, their faith and guidance proceeding before them and on their right: their books.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
Their light proceeds before them and on their right

, that is, their books. God says: As for he who is given his book in his right hand, as for their light, it has guided him. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion we mentioned on the authority of Ad-Dahhak. That is because if he meant by that light the well-known light, he would not have made it specific to the report of striving between the hands and the right without the left, because the light of the believers that they will be given in the Hereafter will illuminate for them everything around them. And in the specific report of God, may He be glorified, about His striving between their hands and on their right without the left, there is what indicates that He meant by it something other than the light, even though they are not devoid of light. The interpretation of the statement, since the matter is as we have described: And to both of them God has promised goodness
h
on the Day you see the believing men and believing women

running, the reward of their faith and righteous deeds before them, and in their right hands the books of their deeds flying about. By his saying strives he means he goes on, and the ba in his saying and their right hands means in.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: the ba in his saying and their right hands means on their right hands. His saying: On the Day you see is from the conjunction of promise. And His statement:
h
Your good tidings today are gardens beneath which rivers flow
. God Almighty says, Your good tidings today, O believers, which you are given good tidings of, are gardens beneath which rivers flow, so rejoice in them. His saying:
h
They will abide therein eternally
means: They will remain in Paradise, never moving from it or being transformed. His saying:
h
That is the great attainment
means: Their eternity in the gardens that he described is the great success that they were seeking after being saved from God’s punishment and entering Paradise to remain there forever.

God Almighty says: It is the great victory on the Day of the hypocrites, men and women. Today is a day of victory for those who believed in God and His Messengers: Look at us. The reciters differed in their recitation of his saying Anzuruna. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa recited it as Anzuruna connected, meaning: wait for us. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as Anzuruna without the alif from Anzurtu meaning: delay us. Al-Farra’ mentioned that the Arabs say Anzurni and they mean: wait for me a little while.

i: He recited in this regard the verse of Amr ibn Kulthum:
x: Abu Hind, do not rush us and wait for us to tell you for sure.

He said: The meaning of this is: Wait a little while and we will tell you, because there is no delay here, but rather listening, like when you say to a man: Listen to me so I can tell you. In my opinion, the correct reading for this is to connect it because this is what is known in the speech of the Arabs when what is meant is we waited and there is no meaning to the delay in this situation, so it is said wait us with the opening of the alif and its hamza. His saying:
h
We take from your light
means: We seek light from your light. The flame is the torch. And His saying:
h
It will be said

, Go back and seek light. He, the Most High, says: They will be answered by saying, ‘Go back from where you came and seek light for yourselves there, for there is no way for you to borrow from Our light.’ And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
On the Day when the hypocrites

, men and women, will say… until His statement: And wretched is the destination. Ibn Abbas said: While the people were in darkness, God sent a light. When the believers saw the light, they headed towards it. The light was a guide from God to Paradise. When the hypocrites saw the believers departing, they followed them, so God cast darkness upon the hypocrites. Then they said, Wait for us, that we may borrow from your light, for we were with you in the world. The believers said, Go back from whence you came from the darkness and seek the light there.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
On the Day when the hypocrites
, men and women, will say to those who believe, the verse: Ibn Abbas used to say while the people were in darkness, then he mentioned something similar. And His statement,
h
Then He placed between them a wall with a door

, inside of which is mercy, but outside of which is torment. God Almighty says, Then God placed between the believers and the hypocrites a wall, which is a barrier between the people of Paradise and the people of Hellfire. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, with a wall with a gate, he said, like the veil in Al-A’raf.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
A wall has been placed between them with a gate
. The wall is a partition between Heaven and Hell.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And a wall will be placed between them with a gate
, he said: This is the wall about which God said, And between them is a veil. It has been said that this wall is in Jerusalem near the Valley of Hell.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me: Al-Hasan bin Bilal told us: Hammad told us: Abu Sinan told us:
m: I was with Ali bin Abdullah bin Abbas at the Valley of Hell, and he narrated on the authority of his father that he said: A wall will be placed between them with a door, inside of which is mercy, but on the outside of which is torment. He said: This is the location of the wall at the Valley of Hell.

c: Ibrahim bin Atiyah bin Radhih bin Atiyah told me: My uncle Muhammad bin Radhih bin Atiyah told me
m: on the
h
On the Day when the hypocrites
, men and women, will say to those who believe, "Wait a moment for us so that we may take some of your light."
h
It will be said

, "Go back and seek light." Then a wall will be placed between them, with a door inside of it, wherein is mercy, but outside of it, on the side of it, is torment. authority of Saeed bin Abdul Aziz on the authority of Abu Al-Awam on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Samit that he used to say: A door whose interior contains mercy and whose exterior contains torment. He said: This is the door of mercy.
b.via: My uncle Muhammad bin Radhih bin Atiyah

c: Ibn Al-Barqi told us: Amr bin Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Atiyah bin Qais, on the authority of Abu Al-Awam,
m: the muezzin of the Holy House, who said: I heard Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-As say: The wall that God mentioned in the Qur’an, and He placed between them a wall with a gate, inside of which is mercy, and outside of which is torment, is the eastern wall, inside of which is the mosque, and outside of which is the valley of Hell.

c: Muhammad bin Awf told me: Abu Al-Mughira told us: Sufyan told us: Shureih told us that
m: Ka’b used to say about the gate in Jerusalem that it is the gate of which God said: And He placed between them a wall with a gate, within it is mercy, but outside it is torment. And His statement, It has a door, its interior contains mercy, God Almighty says: That wall has a door, its interior contains mercy, and its exterior, from the perspective of that exterior, is torment, meaning Hell. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: And its apparent meaning is the torment before it, meaning the Fire.

c: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement,
h
Inside it is mercy
, he said: Paradise and what is in it.

x: And His statement:
h
They will call out to them

, ‘Were we not with you?’ They will say, ‘Yes.’ God the Almighty says: The hypocrites will call out to the believers when a wall has been placed between them, so they remain in darkness and torment, while the believers are in Paradise: Were we not with you in the world, praying and fasting, marrying you and inheriting from you? They will say, Yes. He says: The believers will say, Yes, rather you were like that, but you tempted yourselves and became hypocrites. And their temptation in this instance was hypocrisy. And so said the people of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And you tempt yourselves, he said: Hypocrisy. The hypocrites were with the believers when they were alive, marrying them, cheating on them, and socializing with them, and they were with them when they were dead, and they will all be given the light on the Day of Resurrection, and the light will be extinguished from the hypocrites when they reach the wall, and they will be distinguished from each other at that time. His saying:
h
And you waited
means:
h
And you waited
in faith and defended yourself by acknowledging God and His Messenger.

x: Some of the interpreters said something similar to what we said about this.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:

h

So the interpretation of the speech, according to reading that with emphasis on the two letters: I mean on the sad and the dal, is that the charitable men and women who give charity from their wealth, and loan God a goodly loan meaning by spending in His cause and in what He has commanded to spend in or in what He has encouraged, it will be multiplied for them and they will have a noble reward meaning: God will multiply for them the loans that they lent Him and will pay them back their reward on the Day of Resurrection and they will have a noble reward.

And the meaning that the weak reciters have used in their criticism of the short alif does not have much meaning, because what is made of that as report from God and what is diverted from it to report from someone else is not outside of it, all of it, according to its listeners from the people of knowledge, is from the action of God Almighty.

x: God Almighty says: God does not love any arrogant, boastful misers with what they have been given in this world. They are arrogant and boastful about it to people. They are miserly in giving God’s right that He has made obligatory upon them and they are stingy with it. In addition to their stinginess with it, they also command people to be stingy. And His statement,
h
And whoever turns away
, then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy, God Almighty says:
h
And whoever turns away
, averse to the admonition of God, then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy, God Almighty says:
h
And whoever turns away

, averse to the admonition of God, abandoning the work to which He has called him of spending in His cause, rejoicing in what he has been given, arrogant therewith, boastful, miserly, then indeed, God is the One free of his own wealth and spending and of all of His creation, the Praiseworthy to His creation for the blessings He has bestowed upon them.
The Arab scholars differed about the position of the answer to His statement,
h
Those who are miserly and enjoin miserliness on people

Some of them said: It is sufficient to use the report of those like them and for them in the Qur’an, as He said, And if there were a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved or the earth could be split asunder or the dead could be made to speak
r
(Ar-Ra’d: 31)

. There was no report of this position, and God knows best what is revealed, it is as it was revealed or as He intended it to be. Other Arab scholars said: The report has already come in the verse before this, “
h
Those who are miserly and enjoin miserliness on people
h
And whoever turns away

- then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.” He connected two parts to one part and made their answer one, as you say, If you stand up and if you do good, I will give you. He did not delete the report. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement,
h
For God is the Rich
, the Praiseworthy. The majority of the people of Medina read it as,
h
For God is the Rich
, without He from the sentence, and likewise in their copies of the Qur’an without He.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as,
h
For God is the Rich

, the Praiseworthy, without He in the reading, and likewise in their copies of the Qur’an. The correct thing to say is that they are two well-known readings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, For God is the Rich, the Praiseworthy.
The majority of the people of Medina read it as, For God is the Rich, without He from the sentence, and likewise in their copies of the Qur’an without He.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as, For God is the Rich, the Praiseworthy, without He in the reading, and likewise in their copies of the Qur’an.

x: God Almighty says: We have sent with clear explanations and proofs, and We sent down with them the Book with rulings and laws and the balance with justice.

c: As Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: The Book and the Balance. He said: The Balance is justice.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
And We sent down with them the Book and the Balance

, with the truth: The Balance is what people do and deal with in this world of their livelihood, which they take and give. They take with a balance and give with a balance that knows what they take and what they give. He said: The Book contains the religion of the people, which they do and leave. So the Book is for the Hereafter and the Balance is for this world. And His statement:
h
So that people may act justly means that God Almighty says
: So that people may act justly among themselves. And His statement:
h
And We sent down iron

, in which is great force. God Almighty says: And We sent down for them iron, in which is great force. He says: It has great strength. And benefits for the people. This is what they benefit from when they meet the enemy and other benefits from it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Ahmar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Three things descended with Adam, may God’s prayers be upon him: the anvil, the two bitches, the hammer, and the sword.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
And We sent down iron
, in which is great force, he said: Great force is the swords and weapons with which people fight, and benefits for people, after they dig with it the earth and mountains and other things.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
And We sent down iron
, in which is great power and benefits for people, and a shield and a weapon, and He sent it down so that God might know who would support Him. And His statement:
h
And that God may know who supports Him and His messengers in secret

, God Almighty says: We sent Our messengers to Our creation and sent down these things with them so that they may be just between them and so that the party of God may know who supports the religion of God and His Messenger in secret from Him. And His saying: Indeed, God is Powerful and Exalted in Might. God Almighty says: Indeed, God is Powerful in taking revenge on those who openly display enmity and disobey His commands and prohibitions. He is Exalted in taking revenge on them. No one is able to take revenge on Him from the punishment He has permitted.

x: God Almighty says: “And We sent, O mankind, Noah to Our creation and Abraham, his friend, to them as a messenger. And We placed among their descendants prophethood and the Book.” And thus was prophethood among their descendants, and upon them were revealed the books: the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, the Criterion, and all the other well-known books. And among them is he who is guided. He says: Among their descendants is he who is guided to the truth and has insight. And many of them, meaning among their descendants, are wicked, meaning misguided, departing from the obedience of God to His disobedience.

God Almighty says: Then We followed in their footsteps with Our messengers whom We sent with clear proofs, in the footsteps of Noah and Abraham with Our messengers, and We followed with Jesus, son of Mary. And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him meaning: those who followed Jesus according to his method and law kindness and He is the most merciful and mercy and monasticism, which they innovated meaning: they invented it.
h
We did not prescribe it for them

meaning: We did not impose that monasticism upon them except seeking the pleasure of God meaning: but they innovated it seeking the pleasure of God so they did not observe it with its right observance.
The interpreters differed regarding those who did not observe monasticism properly.
Some of them said: They are the ones who invented it and did not practice it, but they changed and contradicted the religion of God with which Jesus was sent, so they became Christians and Jews.

Others said: Rather, they are a people who came after those who invented it, but they did not observe it properly because they were infidels. Rather, they said, We will do as those who were first to do it. So they are the ones whom God described as not observing it properly. In a manner similar to what we said in the interpretation of these letters to the point where we mentioned that the people of interpretation differed in that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told me: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy. These two are from God. Monasticism was invented by a people from among themselves and was not prescribed for them, but they sought thereby and desired the pleasure of God, but they did not observe it as it should be observed. It was mentioned to us that they rejected women and took monasteries.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And monasticism which they innovated. He said: It was not prescribed for them. They innovated it seeking the pleasure of God.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
We did not prescribe it for them

, he said, Then why? He said, They innovated it, seeking the pleasure of God voluntarily, but they did not observe it as it should be observed. It was mentioned that those who did not observe monasticism properly were not the ones who invented it, but they were the ones who should be emulated. Al-Husayn ibn al-Harith Abu Ammar narrated: Al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated from Sufyan from Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib from Sa’id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas, who said: There were kings after Jesus who changed the Torah and the Gospel, and among them were believers who read the Torah and the Gospel. It was said to their king: We do not find anything more severe for us than the insults that these people insult us with, that they read: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers (al-Ma’idah 5:44). These verses, along with what they criticize us for in their recitation, so call them, let them recite as we recite and believe as we believe in it. He said: So he called them and gathered them and offered them death or to abandon the recitation of the Torah and the Gospel except what they changed from them. They said: What do you want? So leave us. He said: A group of them said: Build us a pillar and raise us to it, then give us something to raise our food and drink with, so that we will not be thrown back to you.

x: A group of them said: Let us wander in the land and wander and drink as wild beasts drink. If you gain control over us in your land, kill us.

A group said: Build us houses in the deserts, and we will dig wells and cultivate vegetables, so that we will not come back to you or pass by you. There is no one among them who does not have a close friend among them. He said: So they did that, so God, the Most High, revealed: “And monasticism, which they invented for themselves.
h
We did not prescribe it for them

except seeking the pleasure of God, but they did not observe it with its right observance.” The others said: We will worship as so-and-so worships, and we will travel as so-and-so travels, and you will build houses as so-and-so did, and they were in their polytheism, having no knowledge of the faith of those who followed them. He said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent and only a few of them remained, a man descended from his monastery, a traveler came Then We followed up their footsteps with Our messengers, and followed up with Jesus, the son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel and placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy and monasticism, which they innovated.
h
We did not prescribe it for them

except seeking the pleasure of God, but they did not observe it with its right observance. So We gave those who believed among them Their reward, and many of them are wicked. from his travels, and the owner of the house came from his house, and they believed in him and confirmed him. So God, the Most High, said: “
h
O you who have believed

, fear God and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion of His mercy.” He said: Two rewards for their belief in Jesus and their belief in the Torah and the Gospel, and their belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their belief in him. He said: And He will make for you a light by which you will walk. The Qur’an and their following the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And peace and blessings be upon him, he said: “So that the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of God and that bounty is in the hand of God.

He gives it to whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty.” (al-Hadid 57:29) Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated: Dawud ibn al-Muhbir narrated: al-Sa’aq ibn Hazn narrated: Aqil al-Ja’di narrated: Abu Ishaq al-Hamadani narrated: Suwaid ibn Ghafla narrated: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Those who came before us differed into seventy-one sects, three of which were saved and the rest perished. One of the three sects challenged the kings and fought them over the religion of God and the religion of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, so the kings killed them. Another sect did not have the strength to challenge the kings, so they stayed among their people, calling them to the religion of God and the religion of the son of Mary, peace be upon him, so the kings killed them and sawed them through with saws. Another sect did not have the strength to challenge the kings or to stay among their people, calling them to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus, peace be upon him, so they fled to the wilderness and mountains and became monastics there.
This is the saying of God, the Almighty: And monasticism which they invented for themselves,
h
We did not prescribe it for them

. He said: They did it only seeking the pleasure of God. “So what…” They took care of it as it should be taken care of.” He said: Those who came after them did not take care of it as it should be taken care of. “So We gave those among them who believed their reward.” He said: They are those who believed in Me and believed Me. He said: And many of them are wicked. He said: They are those who denied Me and called Me a liar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And monasticism, which they invented for themselves, which we did not write down.

x: Others said that those who worshipped from among the polytheists and those who were destroyed among them say, We worship as so-and-so worships and we wander as so-and-so wanders, while they are in their polytheism and have no knowledge of the faith of those who follow their example.
Mention of those who said that those who did not take care of it properly are the ones who invented it.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy to the words the observance of which is due

. He says: They did not obey me in it and spoke therein in disobedience to God. This is because God, the Almighty, prescribed fighting for them before He sent Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him. Then when the people of faith were expelled and only a few of them remained and the polytheists increased in number and the messengers were gone and were subjugated, they secluded themselves in caves. This continued with them until a group of them disbelieved and abandoned the command of God, the Almighty, and His religion and took to innovation, Christianity and Judaism, but they did not observe them as they should be observed.

x: A group remained steadfast in the religion of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, when he came to them with clear proofs and God, the Almighty, sent Muhammad as a Messenger, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and they were like that. This is what His statement: “
h
O you who have believed
, fear God and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion of His mercy” to And God is Forgiving and Merciful.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd narrated to us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: Concerning His statement, And monasticism, which they innovated for themselves,
h
We did not prescribe it for them

, God, the Almighty, had prescribed fighting for them before He sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then when the people of faith were expelled and only a few of them remained, and the polytheists increased in number and the messengers were cut off, they isolated themselves from the people and became ghouls. They remained like that until a group of them changed their ways and abandoned the religion of God, His command and His covenant which He had enjoined upon them, and they adopted innovations, so they innovated Christianity and Judaism. Then God, the Almighty, said to them, They did not observe them with their right observance, and a group of them remained steadfast in the religion of Jesus, may God bless him and grant him peace, until God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they believed in him.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us: Zakariya ibn Abi Maryam told us:
m: I heard Abu Umamah al-Bahili say: God has prescribed for you the fasting of Ramadan, but He has not prescribed for you the standing in prayer during it. Rather, standing in prayer

evidence.text: These verses, along with what they criticize us for in their recitation, so call them, let them recite as we recite and believe as we believe in it.
He said: So he called them and gathered them and offered them death or to abandon the recitation of the Torah and the Gospel except what they changed from them.

x: God Almighty says:
h
O you who have believed

in God and His Messenger from among the People of the Two Scriptures, the Torah and the Gospel, fear God by performing His obedience and avoiding His disobedience and believe in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
O you who have believed
, fear God and believe in His Messenger, meaning those who believed among the People of the Book.
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
O you who have believed
, fear God and believe in His Messenger, meaning those who believed from among the People of the Book. And His statement,
h
He will give you a double portion of His mercy

, means He will give you double the reward for your belief in Jesus, peace and blessings be upon him, and the prophets before Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and then your belief in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, when he was sent as a prophet. The root of the word kafl is fortune, and its root is what a rider holds onto, holding him back and protecting him from falling. He says, This kafl protects you from punishment, just as a kafl protects a rider from falling. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Abu Ammar Al-Marwazi told us: Al-Fadl bin Musa told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
He will give you a double portion of His mercy

. He said: Two rewards for their belief in Jesus, peace and blessings be upon him, and their belief in the Torah and the Gospel, and their belief in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and their belief in him. He said: Ibn Hamid told us:

c: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
He will give you a double portion of His mercy

. He said: Two rewards: their belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their belief in Jesus, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Torah and the Gospel. And on his authority, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Harun bin Antara, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He will give you two portions of His mercy, he said: two rewards.

c: Ali told us: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He will give you double of His mercy
, meaning: double. He said: Mihran told us:

c: Yaʿqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Jaʿfar with seventy horsemen to the Negus to invite him. He came to him and invited him, and the Negus responded to him and believed in him. When he was about to return, some of those who had believed in him from his kingdom, and they were forty men, said: Give us permission to go to this Prophet and greet him and help these people at sea, for we know the sea better
h
O you who have believed
, fear God and believe in His Messenger.
h
He will give you a double portion of His mercy

and make for you a light by which you will walk and forgive you. And God is Forgiving and Merciful. than they do. So they came with Jaʿfar to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had prepared for the Battle of Uhud. When they saw the hardship and difficulty of the Muslims, they asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for permission. They said: O Prophet of God, we have wealth and we see the hardship of the Muslims. If you give us permission, we will return, bring our wealth, and help the Muslims with it. So he gave them permission and they returned, brought their wealth, and helped the Muslims with it. Then God revealed about them: Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they believe in it. (al-Qasas 28:52) And from what We have provided them they spend (al-Qasas 28:54). This was the spending with which they helped the Muslims. When the People of the Book heard from those who did not believe in His saying,
h
They will be given their reward twice over for what they patiently endured (al-Qasas 28

:54), they fell down on the Muslims and said, “O group of Muslims, as for he among us who believes in your Book and our Book, he will have his reward twice over, and he who does not believe in your Book will have a reward like your rewards. What is your superiority over us?” Then God revealed, “
h
O you who have believed
, fear God and believe in His Messenger.
h
He will give you a double portion of His mercy

.” So He made their reward for them and increased them in light and forgiveness. Then He said, lest the People of the Book know and this is how Saeed bin Jubayr read it, lest the People of the Book know that they have no power over anything.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
He will give you double of His mercy
, he said: double.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
He will give you a double portion of His mercy
. He said: The two portions are two rewards for their first faith and for the Book that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought.
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: In His statement,
h
O you who have believed
, fear God and believe in His Messenger, meaning those who believed from among the People of the Book,
h
He will give you a double portion of His mercy
, he said: A reward for your belief in the first book and the one brought by Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement,
h
He will give you a double portion of His mercy
, he said: Two rewards, the reward of this world and the reward of the Hereafter.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Sufyan, who said: Anbasa told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abu Musa:
m: He will give you double portions of His mercy. He said: The double portions are double the reward in the language of Abyssinia.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: “People will be divided into four categories on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:a man who believed in Jesus and then believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will have two rewards; a man who disbelieved in Jesus and then believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will have one reward; a man who disbelieved in Jesus and then disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he incurred wrath upon wrath; and a man who disbelieved in Jesus from among the polytheists of the Arabs and died in his disbelief before Muhammad, so he incurred wrath.”

c: Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid told me: My father told me:
m: I asked Saeed bin Abdul Aziz about the guarantee, how much is it? He said: Three hundred and fifty good deeds, and the two guarantees are seven hundred good deeds. Saeed said: Omar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him asked one of the Jewish rabbis, how much is the best of what you have doubled for you as a good deed? He said: The guarantee is three hundred and fifty good deeds. Omar praised God for giving us two guarantees, then Saeed mentioned the words of God the Almighty in Surat Al-Hadid, He will give you two guarantees from His mercy. I said to him: The two guarantees on a Friday are like this? He said: Yes. In a similar manner to what we have said about this, the hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is authentic.

x: Who said that?

c: Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Muammar ibn Rashid told us, on the authority of Firas, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three who will be given their reward twice: a man who believed in the first book and the second book; a man who had a mother and educated her and educated her well, then freed her and married her; and a slave who worshipped his Lord well and was sincere to his master.”

c: Yaqub told me: Ibn Abi Zaydah told us: Salih ibn Salih al-Hamdani told me, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Abu Musa, on the authority of Abu Musa, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Samad told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Salih bin Salih,
m: who heard Al-Sha’bi narrating on the authority of Abu Burdah, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

evidence.text: Then He said, lest the People of the Book know and this is how Saeed bin Jubayr read it, lest the People of the Book know that they have no power over anything.

x: God Almighty says: To the believers in Him and in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among the People of the Book, your Lord will do this to you so that the People of the Book may know that they are not able to do anything of the bounty of God which He has given you and made you special with, because they thought that God had given them preference over all of creation. So God, may He be glorified and exalted, informed them that He had given the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the bounty and honor that He had not given them, and that the People of the Book envied the believers when the verse was revealed: “
h
O you who have believed

, fear God and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion of His mercy and provide for you a light by which you will walk and will forgive you. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.” So God Almighty said: I did that so that the People of the Book may know that they are not able to do anything of the bounty of God.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
O you who have believed

, fear God and believe in His Messenger… the verse. He said, When this verse was revealed, the People of the Book envied the Muslims for it, so God, the Almighty, revealed, “So that the People of the Scripture will not know that they have no power… the verse. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say, ‘Our example and the example of the People of the Two Scriptures before us is that of a man who hired laborers to work until the night for one qirat. When it was noon, they grew tired of his work and grew fed up, so he settled the account with them and paid them according to that amount. Then he hired laborers until the night for two qirats to work for him the rest of his work. It was said to him, What is the matter with these people who work the least and are paid the most? He said, Why do I give to whomever I wish? I hope that we will be the ones with the two qirats.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada,
m: Two portions of His mercy. He said: It has reached us that when it was revealed, the People of the Book envied the Muslims, so God revealed, So that the People of the Book will not know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of God.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: Abu Ammar told us, he said: Al-Fadl bin Musa told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: So that the People of the Scripture who are eavesdropping will not know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of God.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly. It was said that lest he know is lest he know. It was mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah, it is lest the People of the Book know that they will not be able, because the Arabs make la a connective in every statement that has at the beginning or end a denial that is not explicit, like his saying in the previous denial that was not explicit, What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you? (al-A’raf 7:12), and his saying, And what makes you perceive that when it comes they will not believe? (al-An’am 6:109), and his saying, And it is forbidden for a city which We have destroyed
r
(Al-Anbiya’: 95)
… the verse, and the meaning of that is: We destroyed them. We said about that what the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Abu Harun al-Ghanawi told us: Khattab bin Abdullah said:
m: So that the People of the Book will not know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of God. He said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us on the authority of Abu al-Mu’alla, who said: Sa’id ibn Jubayr used to say: So that the People of the Book may not know and His statement, and that bounty is in the hand of God means, the Most High said: And so that they may know that bounty is in the hand of God, not them or anyone else among creation. He gives it to whomever He wills So that the People of the Scripture will know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of God and that the bounty is in the hand of God. He gives it to whom He wills. And God is the possessor of great bounty. means He gives that bounty to whomever He wills among His creation. That is not for anyone other than Him. And God is the possessor of great bounty means, the Most High said: And God is the possessor of great bounty over His creation.

notes.en: The author reported it in his Tārīkh (1/130). The wording ‘the mīqaʿah and the hammer’ is as transmitted; it counts four items, not three. Compare al-Qurṭubī’s Tafsīr (17/261), citing al-Thaʿlabī from Ibn ʿAbbās: ‘Adam descended from Paradise with five iron objects…’ including the mīqaʿah and hammer. Al-Ṭūsī in al-Tibyān (9/532) reads: ‘God sent down with Adam the tools—the anvil, hammer, and tongs—from heaven.’ Al-Qurṭubī also cites ʿIkrimah from Ibn ʿAbbās: ‘…the mīqaʿah, that is, the hammer.’ Ibn Kathīr (8/54) reads ‘…the mīqaʿah, meaning the hammer,’ and attributes it to the author and Ibn Abī Ḥātim. Al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr (1/56) attributes the wording ‘the anvil, tongs, and hammer’ to them. See Maʿānī al-Qurʾān by al-Farrāʾ (3/136) and Tāj al-ʿArūs, root w-q-ʿ.

notes.en: T2 and T3 read ‘in order that not.’ The wording li-kaylā is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Salamah, not Ibn Jubayr. It is also reported that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, Ibn Jubayr, and ʿIkrimah—as cited in al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ—read ‘so that He may know.’ Mukhtaṣar Shawādhdh lists Ibn ʿAbbās instead of Ibn Jubayr for this transmission. See Mukhtaṣar Shawādhdh, p. 153, and al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ, 8/229.
notes.ar: في ت 2، ت 3: "كيلا". وقوله: (لكيلا) وردت به الرواية عن ابن عباس وعبد اللَّه بن أبي سلمة لا عن ابن جبير، وورد أيضًا أن عبد اللَّه بن مسعود وابن جبير وعكرمة - كما في البحر المحيط - قرءوا: (لكي يعلم). وفي مختصر الشواذ ذُكر ابنُ عباس مكان ابن جبير في هذه الرواية. مختصر الشواذ ص 153، والبحر المحيط 8/ 229.
